# CITY, IN EVERYDAY GESTURES

## Publication identity

- Title: CITY, IN EVERYDAY GESTURES
- Subtitle: Washington, D.C., 1942
- Photographer line: Photographs by Gordon Parks
- Editorial descriptor: An archival selection
- Publication form: contemporary digital sample book
- Audience: adults interested in city neighborhoods, daily life and labor
- Cover form: front cover
- Interior form: flat, upright facing-page spreads
- Source page proportion: 1600 by 2000
- Source combined-spread proportion: 3200 by 2000
- Source spread format: PNG
- Page ratio: 4:5
- Spread ratio: 8:5
- Inner reading margin: at least 5% of page width on each side of the central gutter
- Folio basis: sample sequence numbers
- Editorial language: English
- Documentary image inventory: P01–P10, ten photographs
- Recorded date span: June–November 1942
- Recorded months represented: June, July, August, November 1942
- Text source: original editorial abstracts of catalog records and visible photographs
- Photograph collection: Library of Congress FSA/OWI
- Photograph credit: Gordon Parks / Library of Congress, FSA/OWI
- Caption fields: image ID; neutral caption label; recorded place; month/year; photograph credit
- Additional crop label: Detail

## Chapter aims

| Number | Chapter | Photograph group | Editorial aim |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 01 | Work in view | P01, P02, P09 | Different forms of labor: a demolition-site instruction, government cleaning and fuel service; separate recorded work settings. |
| 02 | Daily provisions | P03, P04, P05 | A grocery store, a shopper and a home table; an editorial association between different settings for daily provisions. |
| 03 | Being together | P06, P07, P08, P10 | A birthday table, two children, a dance group and two waterfront figures; distinct occasions and forms of togetherness. |

- Place: Washington, D.C.

- Visible detail: a tool resting across the laborer's shoulder
- Recorded identification: unnamed laborer in a work setting
- Credit: Gordon Parks / Library of Congress, FSA/OWI
- Archive record: https://hdl.loc.gov/loc.pnp/fsa.8b14795
- Official Flickr record: https://www.flickr.com/photos/library_of_congress/51132694567

- Archive record: https://hdl.loc.gov/loc.pnp/fsa.8d23362

## Source provenance

- Supplied files: ten JPEGs downloaded directly from the Library of Congress official Flickr account
- Download state: original files with original framing and encoding
- Date basis: catalog dates
- Collection advisory: no known restrictions
- Collection Rights & Access status: public domain; free to use and reuse
- P03 and P08 source relationship: Gordon Parks records referring to same-number government negatives in the LC-USF34 series
- P03 and P08 transparency advisory scope: images copied from outside sources
- Retained source-project records: original catalog records, download URLs, SHA-256 hashes and visual inspection notes
- Editorial materials: original commission text, chapter notes and archival abstracts

steps.userMessage:
CITY, IN EVERYDAY GESTURES | An archival image book about everyday life and labor

We are developing a digital publication sample for adults interested in city neighborhoods and everyday labor. The front cover must print "CITY, IN EVERYDAY GESTURES", the subtitle "Washington, D.C., 1942", the photographer line "Photographs by Gordon Parks" and the descriptor "An archival selection". Its documentary content is the ten supplied Gordon Parks photographs, P01–P10, from the Library of Congress FSA/OWI collection. Their recorded dates span June–November 1942. The three chapters are 01 — Work in view, 02 — Daily provisions and 03 — Being together. The supplied archival abstracts provide the editorial text; the reading order within each chapter is open.

The sample consists of a front cover and flat, upright facing-page spreads. Each page has a 4:5 proportion and each complete spread an 8:5 proportion, with a reading margin of at least 5% of page width on each side of the central gutter. Use a typography-led cover and one consistent system for chapter headings, folios and captions. Every photograph on an opener or narrative spread carries its ID, neutral caption label, recorded place, month/year and the credit Gordon Parks / Library of Congress, FSA/OWI. A shared credit may cover all photographs on one spread. Each assigned photograph appears with its complete photographed scene intact at least once in that artwork, preserving its monochrome appearance, orientation, proportions and depicted contents. Additional crops carry the label "Detail". Editorial bridges identify visual associations between separate records, with each photograph retaining its own date and setting.

Audience: the editorial and design team, choosing the publication's narrative structure and a page system for adult readers interested in urban life.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the fixed publication wording, chapter aims, archival abstracts and photograph records.
02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists every deliverable's proportion, format and stage.
P01.jpg is an identity source showing Laborer on Independence Avenue.
P02.jpg is an identity source showing Ella Watson, government cleaner.
P03.jpg is an identity source showing J. Benjamin’s grocery store.
P04.jpg is an identity source showing Shopper on Saturday afternoon.
P05.jpg is an identity source showing Dinner on Lamont Street.
P06.jpg is an identity source showing Lemonade on Seaton Road.
P07.jpg is an identity source showing Children at Frederick Douglass housing project.
P08.jpg is an identity source showing Dance group at Frederick Douglass housing project.
P09.jpg is an identity source showing Amoco mechanic.
P10.jpg is an identity source showing Two familiar faces on the waterfront.
reading-geometry.png is the constraint drawing for page proportions, spread proportions and the central reading margin.
empty-reading-room.png is an atmosphere reference for quiet adult reading and display.

Deliverables:
1. One finished front cover with the title, subtitle, photographer line and editorial descriptor
2. Two chapter-opening spreads: 01 — Work in view using P01, and 02 — Daily provisions using P03, each with its chapter aim adapted into a short introduction
3. Three narrative spreads: Work in view using P01, P02 and P09; Daily provisions using P03, P04 and P05; Being together using P06, P07, P08 and P10, each with complete captions and an editorial bridge of 30–50 words

Acceptance:
- The front cover prints CITY, IN EVERYDAY GESTURES, Washington, D.C., 1942, Photographs by Gordon Parks and An archival selection with the spelling given above.
- The two chapter-opening spreads and three narrative spreads use 4:5 pages within 8:5 spreads, at least 5% inner reading margins, and matching heading, folio and caption systems.
- The chapter-opening spreads and narrative spreads contain their assigned photograph sets; each assigned image has one intact full-scene appearance and retains its monochrome appearance, orientation, proportions and contents.
- Every photograph on the five spreads has its P01–P10 ID, neutral caption label, place, month/year and Gordon Parks / Library of Congress, FSA/OWI credit matching 01-client-facts.en.md.
- Each of the three narrative spreads contains a 30–50-word editorial bridge; its chapter grouping and factual statements follow the chapter aims and individual records in 01-client-facts.en.md.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
